input.rationale: With only 3 merit measurements, I tested compositions based on priors about BiVO4 and copper vanadate. The composition most like BiVO4 (idx 3, Bi0.40Cu0.19V0.41) gave only 3.1e-7 A. Idx 8 (Bi0.18Cu0.34V0.48) gave 1.29e-6 A. That composition is near a BiVO4 plus copper vanadate mixture; copper vanadate absorbs more at 2.4 eV. Moving further toward the Cu/V side (idx 95, Bi0.14Cu0.40V0.46) gave 1.18e-6 A, slightly lower. So the peak appears to lie near idx 8.

rejected.reason: Measured 3.1e-7 A. The Bi-rich, BiVO4-like region is about 4x lower than idx 8.
Measured 1.18e-6 A, slightly below idx 8. Adding more Cu past idx 8 did not help.

content.text:
I submitted **index 8 (Bi 0.18, Cu 0.34, V 0.48)**, which gave the highest photocurrent I measured: **1.29 µA**. The submission was accepted.

The merit budget was only 3 measurements, so I picked all three from prior knowledge of these materials rather than a data-driven search:

| Index | Bi / Cu / V | Photocurrent | Why I picked it |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | 0.40 / 0.19 / 0.41 | 0.31 µA | Closest to BiVO4 (bismuth vanadate), a known photoanode |
| 8 | 0.18 / 0.34 / 0.48 | **1.29 µA** | Roughly BiVO4 mixed with a copper vanadate, which absorbs more light at 2.4 eV |
| 95 | 0.14 / 0.40 / 0.46 | 1.18 µA | Continues the trend toward more Cu and less Bi |

Moving from index 3 to index 8 increased the photocurrent about 4 times. Going a step further to index 95 dropped it slightly, which suggests the best region is near index 8. That rests on only three points, though, and most of the 138 candidates were never measured, so a better composition could still be in the library.

- **XRD not used:** none of the 5 XRD measurements were spent, so which crystal phases are present is inferred from composition, not confirmed.
- **Phase list not read:** the phase list was too large to open.
- **GP suggestion overridden:** for the last measurement I chose index 95 by following the trend instead of the model's pick (index 4).
